photos.desc: In the spring, sharp-tailed grouse form mating grounds, or leks, where they congregate to compete for territories and perform mating displays for visiting females. This crowded scene leads to fighting

A sharp-tailed grouse nest in South Dakota prairie. Photo Credit: Tom Koerner/USFWS

Groups of male sharp-tailed grouse choose a gathering place, called a lek, where they dance, strut and display their plumage to attract females. Upper Souris National Wildlife Refuge, ND Photo: Andy J
